title: Latency hunt — weekly debrief
content:
Attendees: Ava, Diego, Priya, Marta, (notes: Sam dropped in for first 10m)

Objective: weekly sync to triage recent p99 drift observed on shaded nightly bench runs; capture hypotheses, run results, and concrete next steps. This doc is a lightweight log — rough notes + actions.

Summary of current state
- Signal: Over last 48h of nightly shadow runs against mainline commit (commit short: 3a7f2b1) we see 25–40% increase in p99 for the mixed-long workload (75% short, 25% 1k+ tok). p50 and p95 flat. Throughput stable.
- Affected configs: A100-80GB (cuda 12.x), hparams: batch_size_hint=8, async_batcher enabled, kv-cache enabled.
- Repro rate: ~60% in synthetic replay A (mixed-long). Lower (~15%) in production shadowing.

Quick timeline
- 2026-12-12 03:00 UTC — nightly shadow-run finishes, alert triggered (p99 > SLA threshold)
- 2026-12-13 — bench triage; initial bisect pointed to kernel-selection tweak (PR GH#1429) that landed on 2026-12-11
- 2026-12-14 — team run extended stress sessions across multiple seeds and two hardware pools (A100 and H100)

What we ran this week (short list of runs)
- run_id: hunt-20261214-a (A100, mainline 3a7f2b1, async_batcher on) — mixed-long 6h, p99 shifted +32% vs baseline; tail spikes correlated with 1–2s micro-pauses on host 10.42.1.7
- run_id: hunt-20261214-b (H100, same commit) — p99 +12%, variance higher but fewer tail spikes; hints at hardware sensitivity
- run_id: hunt-20261214-c (A100, reverted kernel-selection to pre-PR) — p99 normal, indicates PR is suspect but not definitive (difference reduced after warmup)
- run_id: hunt-20261214-d (A100, disable async_batcher) — p99 returns closer to baseline, throughput drops ~8%

Initial hypotheses (ranked quick)
1) Kernel-selection change (GH#1429) toggles a code path that increases memcopy contention under async batching and long sequences. Evidence: revert run returns baseline.
2) Async_batcher heuristics + kv-cache interaction cause uneven queueing (long requests delaying small ones) that manifests as tail outliers. Evidence: disabling async_batcher reduces tail but impacts throughput.
3) Host-level noise (scheduling/IO) amplified by a new spinlock in kernel path — observed 1–2s micro-pauses on one host; but not consistent across hosts.
4) Model compilation flags changed (quantization/fast-attn) that are sensitive to sequence length and kernel selection; shows hardware-dependent effect.

Observations and evidence details
- Flame graphs from hunt-20261214-a show increased time in memcpy_h2d and memcpy_d2h around tail events; CPU-side thread blocked waiting on device transfer at ~98th percentile.
- Batcher queue traces show bursts where a long request (1k tokens) arrives and grows the in-flight set, pushing a few small requests into a slower execution path when using async_batcher. We can reproduce this by seeding the synthetic driver with a forced long-request at specific intervals.
- Host 10.42.1.7 had elevated NIC interrupts during one of the windows — correlates with one of the p99 spikes; other hosts did not show same pattern.
- H100 runs show smaller delta; suggests kernel selection may pick different kernels or have different concurrency characteristics on H100.

Decisions made in sync
- Short-term rollback allowed: revert kernel-selection change in a canary pool for 24h while we collect more shadow samples. Diego to open canary rollout (GH:revert-1429-canary).
- Run a focused microbench that isolates memcopy path: use synthetic worker that issues long-seq-only workload to measure memcpy latency distribution (Priya to run on both A100 and H100).
- Instrument async_batcher to emit a lightweight event when queue depth > threshold and when a long request is batched with > N small requests (Marta to add telemetry hook).
- Add host-level telemetry correlation to the bench pipeline (interrupt rates, irq balance, suspend/resume events). Sam volunteers to help map kernel logs to bench windows.

Open action items (owners + eta)
- Diego: create canary revert rollout + smoke checks, link: GH:repo/serving-runtime#revert-1429-canary. ETA: 2026-12-15 EOD.
- Priya: run memcpy microbench across A100/H100 + upload flame graphs to the bench artifact store. ETA: 2026-12-16.
- Marta: add async_batcher queue telemetry (emit event with 'long_count', 'small_count', 'queue_depth'). Minimal safe hook to avoid perf impact. ETA: 2026-12-17 (PR draft by EOD 12-15).
- Ava: correlate host interrupt/NIC metrics with run windows; produce a short appendix of correlated hosts. ETA: 2026-12-16.
- Diego + Priya: plan a follow-up 30-minute deep dive on 2026-12-17 to decide whether kernel-selection patch needs modification vs full revert.

Notes to follow-ups / experiments to schedule
- A/B variant: modify kernel-selection to prefer h2d/d2h coalescing path (experiment flag) rather than full revert; test effect on p99 and throughput.
- Batcher experiment: cap long-request coalescing window (e.g., 50ms) to reduce chances a long request absorbs multiple small ones into the same batch. Measure throughput loss vs p99 improvement.
- Shadowing plan: increase production shadow sample size for 48h to check real-world incidence (current low production repro likely due to lower long-request fraction).

Unresolved questions / parking lot
- Why did the initial CI/nightly checks not catch this? Hypothesis: baseline workloads used did not include enough long sequences; we need an explicit mixed-long test in nightly benchmarks.
- Is memcopy contention a symptom (downstream) or root cause (kernel path change introduced extra memcpy)? Need microbench to decide.
- Could NVSwitch topology or PCIe scheduling on some boxes be amplifying signals? Need host-level hardware affinity map.

Quick checklist for next 48h
- [ ] Canary revert + collect shadow samples (Diego)
- [ ] Memcpy microbench + flame graphs (Priya)
- [ ] Async_batcher telemetry (Marta)
- [ ] Host interrupt correlation (Ava + Sam)
- [ ] 30m deep dive (2026-12-17)
Appendix: quick run metadata (examples)
- hunt-20261214-a: commit=3a7f2b1, hw=A100-80GB, driver=510.xx, cuda=12.2, batch_hint=8, async_batcher=yes, kvcache=yes, duration=6h
- hunt-20261214-c: commit=pre-PR-ker, hw=A100-80GB, duration=3h
- artifact links: bench-store://runs/hunt-20261214-a (flame), bench-store://runs/hunt-20261214-b (traces)

If anything missing or wrong call out in Slack #perf-hunt — will update this doc after deep dive.
